paragraphs: اللهم افتح لي أبواب حكمتك، وانشر عليّ من رحمتك، وعلّمني ما ينفعني، ولا تنسني ما علّمتني، وسهّل عليّ ما استصعبته يا أرحم الراحمين.
اللهم اجعل علمي نافعًا، وصدري منشرحًا، وذهني حاضرًا، واحفظ عليّ ما تعلمت، ووفقني لما تحب وترضى.

sections.title: Anatomy: Temporal fossa, infratemporal fossa & TMJ

questions.stem: Describe the temporomandibular joint regarding its type, articular surfaces, ligaments, movements, and articular disc.
Name the muscles of mastication and state the principal action and nerve supply of each.
List the contents of the infratemporal fossa and organize them by vessels, nerves, muscles, and ligaments.
Explain how the articular disc divides the TMJ and relate each compartment to rotation and translation.
questions.answer: The disc creates upper and lower synovial compartments; translation occurs mainly in the upper compartment and rotation mainly in the lower compartment.

questions.stem: Why is an ointment commonly preferred over a gel for a dry atopic lesion?
questions.answer: Ointments are occlusive, increase hydration of the stratum corneum, and can enhance drug penetration.

questions.stem: Why should topical corticosteroids be used cautiously on infected skin?
questions.answer: Their local immunosuppressive effect can mask or worsen infection unless the infection is treated appropriately.

questions.stem: Why should a potent topical corticosteroid not be used as a general moisturizer?
questions.answer: Unnecessary exposure increases the risk of local adverse effects and systemic absorption without providing routine emollient care.
